title: Is Capitalism Flawed? Fixing and Regulating Free Markets

metadata.title: Is Capitalism Flawed? Fixing and Regulating Free Markets

summary: Eisman and John Cassidy discuss capitalism's critics, Keynesian demand management, monetary targeting, financial incentives and the case for regulated markets. Eisman's recurring emphasis is capital, incentives and factual revision, with an explicit uncertain view of tariff intent. Most historical and political judgments are not trading forecasts.
assessment: Claims are assessed individually. Empirical premises are not treated as successful forecasts. Unverified magnitudes and causal stories remain unresolved; subjective investment judgments are not assigned directional wins.
speaker_map_notes: Steve Eisman interviews John Cassidy. Cassidy supplies most intellectual-history claims; Eisman supplies investment, leverage, fiscal and incentive examples. Shared exchanges retain explicit attribution in the claim or reason.
framework_points: Revise theories when contrary facts persist.
Separate privately profitable incentives from system-wide outcomes.
Evaluate bank gross leverage and capital cushions alongside risk weights.
Preserve innovation while assessing specific market failures; policy preferences are not outcome forecasts.
tools_and_charts: Historical world GDP per person chart is described but not reconstructed.
GDP expenditure identity and net-export arithmetic.
transcript_cautions: Full transcript read, including the complete historical discussion; advertisements and opening montage excluded.
Guest intellectual-history summaries are not Eisman predictions.
The source is published June 23, 2025; contemporary tariff statements are not evaluated as if made at the cutoff.
The Nobel page and FCIC PDF failed full retrieval; no successful verification is claimed from those failed opens.
Some numerical shorthand and personal historical recollections remain unverified.

assumptions: GDP is measured by final domestic expenditures plus exports minus imports.

claims.speaker: John Cassidy
claims.test: Inspect the relevant original financial, operational or economic data and compare the claimed mechanism with competing explanations.

evidence.title: Lifting 800 Million People Out of Poverty
evidence.finding: Joint report finds close to 800 million Chinese people moved above the international $1.90 extreme-poverty line over four decades, with structural transformation and targeted support contributing. This does not establish future escape from the middle-income trap.
